requirement: The platform SHALL support four deployment modes: Enterprise Overlay, Native Identity, Credential/Relying-Party Only, and Sovereign/Dedicated.

Enterprise Overlay SHALL permit authentication and primary lifecycle to remain in the customer's incumbent IdP/directory while Zoiko iD supplies identity mapping, authority, mandates, policy decisions, credentials/signals and evidence.
Tenant identity and cell context SHALL be derived from authenticated trust context and server-side routing; caller-supplied tenant identifiers SHALL never be sufficient authority.
Sensitive identity and authority data SHALL remain within the assigned regional cell unless an explicitly approved cross-region flow exists.
The global control plane SHALL contain only routing/trust metadata required to operate the service and SHALL NOT become a global replica of tenant PII.
Sovereign/Dedicated mode SHALL support dedicated persistence, compute and cryptographic boundaries where contractually required.
Tenant isolation SHALL be enforced at gateway, service, data-access and audit/evidence boundaries, not only through UI filtering.
Plan entitlements and quotas SHALL be centrally enforceable and auditable without weakening security invariants.

Every actor SHALL be represented by an immutable, non-semantic principal_id; email, phone, username, DID, employee number and external IdP subject are identifiers attached to a principal, not the principal key.
The platform SHALL support HUMAN, ORGANIZATION, ORG_UNIT, DEVICE, APPLICATION, SERVICE/WORKLOAD, AI_AGENT and EXTERNAL_PRINCIPAL types with type-specific lifecycle controls.
Identifiers SHALL record type, namespace/issuer, verification state, uniqueness scope, valid time and recorded time.
External identities SHALL be linked using provider/issuer, subject and tenant scope with collision, reassignment and takeover controls.
Automatic high-assurance account linking based only on matching email or telephone number SHALL be prohibited.
Principal lifecycle SHALL support active, suspended, disabled, merged/superseded and deleted/erased states without reusing immutable identifiers.
Security-sensitive principal changes SHALL increment a monotonic security_revision used by authorization and revocation propagation.
Cross-party disclosure SHOULD use pairwise identifiers where global correlation is not required.
Material organization-issued authority SHALL resolve to an AuthorityRootAssertion with a defined assurance class AR-0 through AR-3.
AR-3 roots SHALL support authoritative registry events, vLEI organizational-role credentials and equivalent qualified/certified sources where applicable.
AR-2 roots SHALL support verified board resolutions, corporate-secretary attestations and strong institutional KYB evidence.
AR-0 self-asserted roles SHALL be display-only and SHALL NOT root material authority.
Each root assertion SHALL record source, provenance, freshness, valid time, recorded time, evidence references and refresh policy.
Removal or invalidation of a root SHALL cascade to dependent grants and active mandates according to the applicable R0-R3 revocation SLO.
The platform SHALL distinguish personal grants from role-issued grants so grantor continuity follows ADR-03 semantics.
Registry/provider disagreement SHALL produce an explicit state requiring policy treatment; the platform SHALL NOT silently prefer a stale source.
Native human authentication SHALL support WebAuthn/passkeys as the preferred phishing-resistant method and SHALL support approved step-up factors for higher assurance.
The service SHALL support OIDC/OAuth 2.0, SAML 2.0 and SCIM 2.0 for enterprise interoperability.
OAuth authorization code clients SHALL use PKCE; the implicit flow SHALL NOT be used for production clients.
Sensitive clients and APIs SHALL support sender-constrained access tokens using DPoP or mTLS where required by risk policy.
Session, application session, authorization context and agent mandate execution context SHALL be modeled separately.
Authentication SHALL NOT itself establish organizational/business authority.
Account recovery SHALL be assurance-aware and SHALL support delay, out-of-band notification, re-proofing and dual approval for protected enterprise administrators.
Federation metadata SHALL have expiry, rollover, monitoring and emergency-quarantine behavior; stale signing metadata SHALL NOT be accepted indefinitely.
Native session/token services SHALL support revocation and security_revision checks consistent with the risk-class contract.
Related Origin Requests MAY be used for approved Zoiko multi-domain passkey experiences only after RP-origin governance is documented and tested.
Verification SHALL be provider-neutral; provider outputs SHALL be normalized into canonical VerificationAssertion objects rather than stored as the product domain model.
Verification workflows SHALL support pluggable identity, document, biometric/liveness, address, phone/network, employment/professional and KYB/registry providers as policy requires.
The platform SHALL maintain separate identity, authentication, federation, credential and authority assurance dimensions; they SHALL NOT collapse into one trust score.
Verification assertions SHALL record claim commitment, method, provider/source, assurance profile, jurisdiction, evidence references, performance time, validity, status and provenance.
Reusable verification SHALL require an explicit reliance policy defining eligible relying parties, freshness, liability assumptions, revocation/status handling and retained evidence.
Provider failure SHALL be contained by circuit-breakers and policy-driven fallback; vendor-specific schema failure SHALL NOT corrupt canonical identity state.
Biometric processing SHALL be capability- and jurisdiction-gated, minimized, separately retained and never introduced as an incidental authentication convenience.
The service SHALL expose assurance facts to policy without exposing raw verification evidence to ordinary application callers.
The credential layer SHALL support OID4VCI 1.0, OID4VP 1.0 and HAIP 1.0 for applicable high-assurance interoperability flows.
The platform SHALL support W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 and approved SD-JWT/mdoc profiles where required by ecosystem or jurisdiction.
Zoiko iD SHALL support verifier/relying-party infrastructure as a first-priority role and issuer infrastructure as a separate bounded capability.
A Zoiko-hosted holder/wallet product SHALL NOT be assumed by the verifier core and SHALL require a separate product decision.
Credential status and revocation checks SHALL use privacy-preserving scheme adapters and minimized logging to avoid unnecessary verifier correlation.
Trust federation SHALL baseline OpenID Federation 1.1; wallet-specific draft extensions SHALL remain behind replaceable adapters until finalized.
Credential presentation policy SHALL request only attributes required for the stated purpose and SHALL retain only the minimum evidence needed for the decision class.
QTSP or European Business Wallet provider roles SHALL remain disabled unless separately approved through legal/certification gates.
Every material authorization SHALL be satisfiable by one complete valid authority chain unless an explicit composite-authority policy permits multiple chains.
Delegation SHALL be monotonically attenuating across action, resource, purpose, jurisdiction, data scope, value/count/data limits, time, assurance, tool and delegation depth.
A child grant SHALL NOT widen any parent dimension or outlive the parent/root authority that makes the grant valid.
The policy engine SHALL combine RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC and capability/mandate facts without treating any one model as universally sufficient.
The external PDP contract SHALL use OpenID AuthZEN Authorization API 1.0; internal policy-language choice SHALL remain encapsulated.
Relationship authorization SHALL use revision-consistent projections with a consistency token or equivalent revision reference tied to the authoritative PostgreSQL state.
R2/R3 material actions SHALL use fresh online authorization and SHALL re-evaluate at commit when state can change between preflight and effect.
Risk SHALL be an input that can tighten, step-up or deny; risk SHALL NOT independently grant authority.
Policy decisions SHALL return allow/deny, reason codes, obligations, policy version, relation revision, security revision and expiry/validity context.
Protected policy and authority-administration operations SHALL themselves be subject to strong authorization, separation of duties and evidence receipts.
AI agents SHALL be first-class principals with sponsor/owner, blueprint/type, runtime identity, lifecycle state, allowed tools and delegation policy.
A material delegated agent action SHALL reference an active mandate bound to represented principal, executing principal, permitted resource/action, purpose, tools, time and assurance.
Consumable mandate limits SHALL be managed by an atomic ledger using reserve, commit, release, expiry and reconciliation semantics.
Parallel retries or crashes SHALL NOT permit value/count/data/tool quota double-spend or over-consumption.
Mandate operations SHALL be idempotent using stable transaction/idempotency identifiers.
Sub-agent delegation SHALL be denied unless explicitly allowed and SHALL further attenuate authority and remaining limits.
High-risk mandate actions SHALL support human confirmation/approval obligations before commit.
The public platform SHALL NOT introduce a proprietary ActAs token type. Runtime delegation context SHALL map to stable OAuth/RFC 8693/RAR semantics and an internal Transaction Context Envelope.
Draft transaction-token or identity-chaining protocols SHALL be implemented only behind adapters that can be replaced without changing the public contract.
Mandate completion, exhaustion, revocation, expiry and failed reservations SHALL emit durable lifecycle events and evidence.
The platform SHALL support OpenID Shared Signals Framework, CAEP and RISC for cross-party security-state exchange.
Every enforcement decision SHALL map to a risk class R0, R1, R2 or R3 with a defined freshness and failure posture.
Revocation propagation SHALL be measured end-to-end from authoritative state commit to controlled PEP observation.
R3 state changes SHALL target ≤2 seconds p99 in-cell and ≤5 seconds cross-party where the receiver supports real-time signals; R2 ≤10 seconds; R1 ≤60 seconds; R0 ≤15 minutes.
R2/R3 shall fail closed when policy requires fresh security/authority state and that state cannot be obtained or validated.
Security-state caches SHALL be revision-aware and bounded by risk-class TTL/freshness rules.
Cross-party signal receivers SHALL authenticate, authorize, de-duplicate and replay-protect incoming security events.
Signal publication and receipt SHALL be auditable without storing raw sensitive event payloads beyond necessary retention.
Consent SHALL be a lifecycle object with subject, controller/recipient, purpose, data categories, operations, legal-basis context, notice/policy version, grant/withdrawal and expiry state.
Authorization SHALL consult consent only where consent is a valid and applicable requirement; consent SHALL NOT be treated as a universal legal basis.
Retention SHALL be enforced by a purpose/jurisdiction/class schedule, not by one global tenant retention period.
Legal holds SHALL suspend eligible erasure with a recorded authority/basis, scope and expiry/review date.
Immutable decision receipts SHALL use pairwise/keyed pseudonymous principal handles and commitments; direct PII SHALL be segregated.
Per-subject or otherwise bounded encryption keys SHALL enable cryptographic erasure of segregated subject evidence where legally permitted.
Erasure SHALL include primary stores, derived indexes, caches and backup expiry according to declared windows; deletion SHALL produce verifiable completion evidence.
Data exports and DSAR tooling SHALL enforce requester identity/authority, minimization, redaction and legal retention exceptions.
Security telemetry, audit, evidence and product analytics SHALL remain logically and retention-wise separate purposes.

Material allow/deny decisions SHALL emit a DecisionReceipt containing decision ID/time, pseudonymous actor/represented handles, action/resource class, outcome, reason/obligation codes and relevant revisions.
E2/E3 receipts SHALL include authority/mandate references, assurance/risk state and evidence commitments sufficient to explain the decision without storing raw PII in the receipt.
E3 decisions SHALL preserve deterministic policy inputs needed for forensic replay, signed transaction context and mandate reservation/commit proof.
Receipt intake SHALL use a durable envelope/outbox such that an acknowledged required receipt is not silently lost.
Operator/admin actions SHALL emit auditable receipts; regulated/sovereign lockbox operations SHALL be customer-visible where the product tier requires it.
Evidence objects SHALL support tamper-evident hashing/commitment and WORM-compatible retention by evidence class.
Audit logs SHALL exclude passwords, private keys, session secrets, access tokens, raw biometric payloads and raw credentials.
Policy, schema, relation and evidence version identifiers SHALL remain independently traceable; one application version SHALL NOT substitute for decision reconstruction.
Public, tenant-admin and internal/operator APIs SHALL be separate trust surfaces with independently scoped authorization.
Mutation APIs SHALL require authentication, authorization, schema validation, tenant binding, audit/evidence behavior and idempotency where retry is possible.
All API responses/errors SHALL carry stable request/correlation identifiers and machine-readable error codes.
OpenAPI specifications SHALL be version-controlled and SHALL gate generated SDK compatibility and contract testing.
External callers SHALL NOT directly mutate authority-consumable balances, security revisions or evidence stores outside approved service APIs.
Security-significant state changes SHALL use transactional outbox/event publication; consumers SHALL be idempotent under at-least-once delivery.
Webhook delivery SHALL use signed payloads, replay windows, key rotation, retries and tenant/source scope.
Deprecated API/schema versions SHALL have documented compatibility windows and sunset dates before production removal.
A certification sandbox SHALL provide test credentials, fixtures and automated conformance scenarios without sharing production secrets or data.
No Zoiko human SHALL hold standing production data access; privileged access SHALL be just-in-time, bounded, expiring and attributable to a named operator.
Sensitive support/production access SHALL require dual approval or customer lockbox according to tenant tier and action classification.
Protected tenant-administrator actions SHALL include IdP changes, MFA weakening, bulk export, authority-root changes, credential-signing changes and other security-sensitive configuration.
Protected actions SHALL require step-up authentication, quorum/dual control where defined, a cooling-off delay where appropriate and a decision receipt.
Break-glass access SHALL be separately controlled, time-limited, post-reviewed and incapable of suppressing its own audit/evidence.
Production database owners and service roles SHALL not imply application authorization bypass; least-privilege database roles SHALL be enforced.
Administrative tooling SHALL default to masked/minimized data views and SHALL not expose sensitive payloads merely because the operator is privileged.
Usage SHALL be metered using immutable/reconcilable events sufficient to calculate decisions, verifications, credential operations, receipt classes and other billable units.
Per-tenant quotas and plan entitlements SHALL be enforced independently of authorization safety controls; quota exhaustion SHALL NOT trigger a fail-open security path.
Metering SHALL support dispute reconstruction and correction without rewriting historical usage events.
The platform SHALL support standards-based import/export and tenant exit for identities/relationships/configuration where contractually appropriate.
Offboarding SHALL include federation/SCIM deprovisioning, key and credential retirement, webhooks/integrations closure, data deletion/retention handling and a completion certificate.
Mature Authentication/Token and Authorization PDP services SHALL target ≥99.995% service availability at the defined measurement boundary.
The control/admin plane SHALL target ≥99.9% without becoming a dependency that can weaken runtime authorization when degraded.
R2/R3 authorization SHALL fail closed when fresh mandatory authority/security state or mandate-ledger integrity cannot be confirmed.
Signed access tokens SHALL be locally verifiable by resource servers where policy permits so non-critical authorization-server disruption does not collapse all sessions.
Required decision-receipt envelopes SHALL have a no-acknowledged-loss objective, using durable write/outbox before acknowledgement where the receipt class requires it.
No retry or failover path SHALL produce duplicate authority consumption or mandate double-spend.
Regional authorization p95 SHALL be <40 ms for R0/R1 and <60 ms for R2/R3, excluding external proofing/IdP network calls.
Gateway/authentication context processing SHALL budget ≤10 ms local p95 within the authorization path.
Relationship/attribute reads SHALL budget ≤10 ms R0/R1 and ≤15 ms R2/R3 with revision-aware semantics.
Policy evaluation SHALL budget ≤10 ms R0/R1 and ≤15 ms R2/R3 for the approved Stage A policy complexity profile.
Regional mandate reserve/commit operations SHALL target ≤15 ms p95 for the approved Stage A ledger topology.
Performance results SHALL report p50/p95/p99, saturation, error rate, queue lag and cost per unit; averages alone SHALL NOT be accepted.
Stage A is the initial approved design point: 10M principals, 20k authorization decisions/s global peak, 5k per-cell peak, 10k token issuances/s and 2k R2/R3 receipts/s.
Production-readiness SHALL demonstrate at least 2× the currently approved stage while meeting latency, error, durability and cost constraints.
Stage B (100M / 250k authz/s) and Stage C (500M / 1M authz/s) SHALL remain capacity targets requiring re-ratification before they become production commitments.
Horizontal scaling SHALL not require global synchronous transactions for ordinary tenant operations.
Tenant or cell hot spots SHALL be detectable and containable through partitioning, quota and routing controls.
PostgreSQL tenant shards SHALL remain the transactional source of truth for principals, organizations, grants, mandates, policy metadata and credential/verification metadata.
Relationship stores/graphs SHALL be derived revisioned projections and SHALL NOT independently become authoritative state.
R2/R3 authorization SHALL never produce a new allow from known-stale relation state; the service SHALL use authoritative fallback or deny according to policy.
High-risk consumable limits SHALL be transactionally serialized/atomically guarded; eventual consistency SHALL NOT determine remaining authority.
Security-relevant records SHALL preserve valid time and recorded/system time sufficient to reconstruct what was believed when a decision occurred.
Schema migrations SHALL preserve backward-compatible event/evidence replay for the supported retention window.

Threat models SHALL cover nation-state/APT, organized fraud, malicious tenant admin, compromised/prompt-injected agent, Zoiko insider, supply-chain attacker, coerced operator and compromised trust/registry source.
Security design SHALL include STRIDE and privacy threat analysis (e.g., LINDDUN) for each material plane and new feature class.
Production workloads SHALL use short-lived workload identity/mTLS/federation rather than long-lived static secrets wherever platform support exists.
Private keys and high-value signing keys SHALL be hardware-backed where required, purpose-separated and inaccessible to ordinary application/runtime operators.
Artifacts SHALL be provenance-verifiable with signed builds, SBOMs and a SLSA Build L3-or-stronger target for production release pipelines.
Security-sensitive configuration SHALL be immutable/auditable enough that an attacker with application-level privilege cannot erase the evidence of change.
Secrets, tokens, private keys, raw biometric data and raw credential payloads SHALL be prohibited from ordinary logs.
The threat model SHALL be re-reviewed for every material release and after a significant incident or new high-risk integration.
Token-signing, credential-signing, evidence-signing and encryption keys SHALL be purpose-separated; a single key SHALL NOT serve multiple trust functions.
Key lifecycle SHALL define generation, activation, rotation, overlap, revocation, emergency compromise and destruction for every key class.
Regional and tenant key boundaries SHALL align with the approved residency/isolation tier.
The cryptographic layer SHALL be algorithm-agile so approved post-quantum/hybrid mechanisms can be introduced without rewriting domain services or public APIs.
PQC planning SHALL include ML-KEM/ML-DSA capability and migration criteria for transport and long-lived signatures, without claiming unsupported ecosystem interoperability.
Data minimization SHALL be enforced at collection, API response, logging, evidence and analytics layers.
Direct personal data SHALL NOT be replicated globally merely for operational convenience.
Evidence-class retention SHALL distinguish aggregate, compact, standard and forensic/replay records; higher evidence class SHALL not automatically authorize broader PII retention.
Approved erasure SHALL make Zoiko-controlled PII and resolving keys inaccessible within the declared SLO while preserving non-identifying receipt integrity where legally permitted.
Backups SHALL have bounded retention and demonstrable expiry; 'deleted from primary' SHALL NOT be reported as complete deletion if recoverable copies remain beyond policy.
Core cell services SHALL target RTO ≤15 minutes where paired-region failover architecture is enabled; RPO SHALL be specified per data class and approved before production.
DR SHALL preserve residency boundaries and SHALL NOT route tenant PII into an unapproved jurisdiction during failover.
Recovery exercises SHALL include database, key-service, event-stream, relationship projection and evidence-store scenarios, not only application restarts.
Backups SHALL be encrypted, integrity-checked, restoration-tested and covered by the same key/erasure governance as live data.
Quarterly compromise/DR exercises SHALL be required before Tier-1 availability/resilience claims are used commercially.
Every request SHALL carry request_id/correlation_id and distributed trace context; tenant/cell/service context SHALL be attached in a privacy-safe manner.
Operational metrics SHALL include latency, saturation, errors, queue lag, retry volume, stale-revision rate, revocation propagation and mandate reservation/commit failures.
Security telemetry, audit, evidence and product analytics SHALL use separate schemas/pipelines/retention policies even where they share infrastructure.
SLO breaches for R2/R3 revocation, authorization latency or mandate integrity SHALL page/on-call at severity appropriate to security impact, not only availability impact.
Observability tooling SHALL not require access to raw tenant secrets or raw identity evidence to diagnose normal service health.
Domain schemas, API schemas, event schemas, policy versions, evidence formats and jurisdiction packs SHALL be independently versioned.
Backward-compatible changes SHALL be distinguished from breaking changes and enforced through CI contract tests.
Feature flags MAY control rollout but SHALL NOT override mandatory policy denies or regulatory/security gates.
Every production service SHALL have an accountable owning team, runbook, dependency map and rollback strategy.
No service SHALL access another bounded context's tables directly except through an explicitly approved shared transactional boundary.
Draft standards/protocols SHALL be isolated behind adapters to prevent public-contract lock-in.
Administrative and developer-console surfaces SHALL conform to WCAG 2.2 AA for applicable web UI.
High-risk administrative actions SHALL clearly show actor, target, impact, required approvals and effective time before confirmation.
Error messages SHALL be actionable without leaking sensitive security details to unauthorized users.
Evidence and policy decision explanations SHALL expose human-readable reason/obligation codes while preserving machine-readable canonical codes.
Protocol support SHALL be verified against official conformance/interoperability suites where available before production claims are made.
The architecture SHALL avoid dependence on one verification vendor, cloud, HSM/KMS, wallet or IdP at the domain-model level.
Tenant onboarding and exit SHALL be automatable and documented for standards-based federation/SCIM integrations.
A customer SHALL be able to consume Zoiko authority decisions from an incumbent estate without adopting Zoiko native authentication.
A flow-level controller/processor/independent-controller role map SHALL exist before regulated production for each activated data flow.
Reusable verification SHALL have an approved reliance/liability model before external customers may rely on prior proofing.
SOC 2 Type II control evidence SHALL be designed into access, change, logging, incident and review systems from first production operation.
ISO/IEC 27001 controls SHALL have accountable ownership and evidence collection before regulated enterprise production.
ISO/IEC 27701/27018 requirements SHALL be mapped as privacy/cloud PII scope matures.
UK DVS Trust Framework certification SHALL gate any product claim that Zoiko iD is operating as an in-scope certified UK digital verification service.
EUDI relying-party registration and Member State requirements SHALL gate production wallet interactions where required.
QTSP functionality SHALL remain disabled until qualification/supervision and key-management requirements are formally approved.
FedRAMP SHALL be treated as a US federal-market gate, not a general commercial requirement.
DORA, NIS2, HIPAA, biometric statutes and AI Act obligations SHALL be assessed by feature, customer role and jurisdiction rather than applied generically.
